subject: dartR developer position advertised and open until 22nd of September & new CRAN version is coming

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: dartR developer position advertised and open until 22nd of September & new CRAN version is coming
parts:
Hi everyone,

two good news.

First we were able to get some funding together and are now able to employ a software developer with the aim to support the maintenance and development of the dartR package.

In case you are interested and or know someone suitable that has experience in developing R packages and in wildlife genomics please pass on the link below:

  •  https://uctalent.canberra.edu.au/cw/en/job/494678/software-developer
It is a two year, 0.5 FTE equivalent time position.


The second news is that there will be a new CRAN version of dartR hopefully published in the coming week or so. The new version (around 1.8.3) is currenlty under revision by the gods of CRAN.
The not so good news is that this version was a bit rushed (as we had to deal with orphaned packages vcfR and SNPassoc, which are no longer on CRAN.)


Unfortunately we are  no longer be able to include those packages. Especially the conversion from vcf to genlight is now broken. The good news is that you can still install the vcfR package from thei github pages and use the commented version of the gl.read.vcf funciton in the new version of the package. (just uncommment it and save it) . I will send a description later in the week once accepted by CRAN [fingers crossed].
SNPassoc was mainly used to run HWE tests and a new function gl.hwe.pop which is super fast and runs based on the new HardyWeinberg package is replacing the package and function. It is actually better and has more options in my view. [you can convert the SNP data to use them directly in the HardyWeinberg package which offers several versions to test for HWE.
The new version is already on Github (on the dev branch) the master is still a bit behind as I am tired to update the package and then get a rejection from CRAN.

Otherwise we started the transition to use ggplots instead of base R which should help to get not so many annoying: "Error in plot.new() : figure margins too large"-errors.

Once we have the new developer on board we will be looking for feature requests and also plan to improve some functions which are not really user-friendly and flexible.
E.g. gl.ibd to be used on individuals is on the list.

Sorry for the longer post.
Take care  and in case you know a suitable candidate for the dartR developer please pass the info or let me know.

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: Re: dartR developer position advertised and open until 22nd of September & new CRAN version is coming
parts:
The gods of CRAN have been sympathetic. The new version 1.8.3 is now on CRAN (as the source only) the binaries will take some time to update.

What that means you can wait another week and should be able to simple use:

install.packages("dartR") once CRAN has updated to 1.8.3


Copied from CRAN: You can see there is now the new source, but the binaries are still the old version:

Package source: dartR_1.8.3.tar.gz
Windows binaries: r-devel: dartR_1.1.11.zip,r-release: dartR_1.1.11.zip, r-oldrel: dartR_1.1.11.zip
macOS binaries: r-release: dartR_1.1.11.tgz, r-oldrel: dartR_1.1.11.tgz



or you can use as of now:
library(devtools)
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR")

to get the latest version now.

A little warning: Due to the fact that we are using so many other packages we had to be more strict, which other packages are installed when you installing a package. That means it be faster on install, as not all necessary packages for some special functions will be there. For example the package dismo used to reproject data in the gl.ibd function is not installed automatically. You should get a message, when you want to run gl.ibd and you have not installed the package yet.

If you get a message like: Package dismo needed for this function to work. Please install it.

simply run:
install.packages("dismo") and then the function should run completely.

We had to do this as there are a number of packages that are not maintained and this would break the general install immediately (e.g. the last 5 days you were not able to install from CRAN because of package SNPassoc is no longer on CRAN). So you may need to install some additional packages by hand, depending on the function you use (if they are not already on your system).

For the experts we moved about 10 packages from Depends to Suggests and those is the list of packages that you might have to install by hand if you use a certain function.
Please use either the forum here or Github to report errors you encounter. (which unfortunately might happen)


Cheers, Bernd

Suggests:
    knitr,
    rmarkdown,
    rgl,
    parallel,
    doParallel,
    data.table,
    reshape2,
    pca3d,
    dismo,
    pegas,
    directlabels,
    plotly,
    rgdal,
    leaflet.minicharts,
    leaflet,
    rrBLUP,
    poppr,
    Rcpp,
    igraph,
    qvalue,
    gdistance,
    seqinr,
    pheatmap,
    RColorBrewer
